2.text: The regulations bearing upon birth begin, of course, when the woman is

3.text: first aware that she is with child. From that time on, both the husband

4.text: and the wife must every morning, on awaking from sleep, put on their

5.text: clothes as quickly as possible, go out of the tent, and take a look in

6.text: the direction of the morning dawn. Some make a hasty tour around the

7.text: tent, following the direction of the sun’s course. Not until after that may the

8.text: woman re-enter the inner room to light the lamp. It is desirable that both

9.text: parties should leave their bed together. The woman, however, may go out

10.text: alone; but, if the man wishes to appear first, he must take with him one of

11.text: the boots belonging to his wife. Neglect of any of these particulars will

12.text: make the offspring come slowly, and will cause its flesh to be flabby.

13.text: Moreover, the married couple must not transgress the customary rule that

14.text: places the pillow of the Chukchee bed on the entrance-side of the sleeping-

15.text: room, and which is often ignored by the people.

16.text: The garments for the new-comer are prepared in secret, lest some one

17.text: of the “alien” people should see them. When the clothing for the prospective

18.text: infant is spoken of, it is called “belly-protector,” in order not to use the real word.

19.text: The mother works up to the very last hour. The more active she

20.text: herself is, the stronger and healthier will be her child.

21.text: The husband and the wife sleep together till well nigh the labor-time,

22.text: and there is no restriction against their conjugal life during this period.

23.text: After birth, it is considered more fitting for the husband to have no inter-

24.text: course with the woman for ten days, because, before the expiration of that

25.text: time, the traces of the birth must still remain in the body of the mother.

26.text: On the other hand, if the married couple are desirous of having another child

27.text: as soon as possible (in the event of the first one having died shortly after

28.text: the deliverance), they will have intercourse before the end of this term, and

29.text: this is believed to be conducive to another conception.

30.text: When the time of labor is at hand, no stranger is allowed to enter the

31.text: inner room of the family; and even near relatives of the male sex must keep

32.text: far away, especially if they roam about in the day-time. It is feared that

33.text: some invisible but evil influence will cling to them, and try to approach the

34.text: lying-in woman. When the time of labor begins, all males, not even excepting

35.text: the small children, must leave the sleeping-room, and they must not return
